criteria.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds fixtures of real record kinds: a landed job with invocations, a verifier ending at T, a Landed outcome set at about T+0.1 min, and an athena_data::history::Landing record (commits[].job = the job) with created_at several minutes later, and no HostError. `cargo test -p athena-core status` shows the landing stage equals the minutes from the verifier's end to the later of the outcome and landing.created_at.
criteria.evidence: The test `the_landing_stage_runs_to_the_landing_record_written_after_the_outcome` passed. Its job's verifier ends at 10:17, the Landed outcome follows 0.1 min later, and a real `Landing` record (kind JobLanding, job = the job) has created_at 10:23. The test asserts landing_and_rebuild == 6.0, landing_found, window_with_landing_record == 1 and idle == 0. It uses no HostError. On the base code the stage would be 0.1, so the test fails without the change. A second test, `a_landing_record_of_another_job_does_not_extend_the_landing_stage`, also passed.

findings.summary: No test covers how Records::load reads landing records from the records branch
findings.evidence: Every new test sets `records.landings` directly on a hand-built Records. No store.rs test writes a `landings/<id>.json` to the records branch and checks that Records::load returns it. The reader copies `GitLandingRecords::records_under` (gh/records.rs:109), so it is probably right, but a wrong path or ref would go unnoticed and every job would quietly fall back to its outcome time. The basis line would show that fallback.

findings.summary: Every Records::load now also reads the local records branch, whatever tree it was asked to load
findings.evidence: `Records::load(git, treeish)` now also runs `RecordsWriter::new(git).tip()` plus ls-tree and cat-file on `landings/`. Records::load is called in dozens of places (drain, run, hestia, scope_guard, and others), so each call pays this cost, and a load of a past tree gets current landing records mixed in. A narrower fix is a separate landing loader called only where Throughput is computed (status.rs:1816, hestia.rs:1375). Read errors are also swallowed (`let Ok(..) else return Vec::new()`), so a broken records branch looks the same as 'no landing record'.

findings.summary: An existing test comment still gives the old 'did not land' minutes
findings.evidence: The comment says 'Two jobs that did not land: 30 minutes and 10 minutes of work', but the assertion was changed to `22.0 + 1.0`, the invocation time spent.

summary: The change does what the retry asked. In `athena status`, the landing-and-rebuild time now runs from the verifier's end to whichever is later: the landing outcome or the landing record (`landings/*.json`). The landing record is matched to the job by a JobLanding commit's `job` field. Host refusals play no part, and a job with no landing record falls back to its outcome time, which the printed basis says. "Did not land" and idle time now use time spent (invocation wall times, check durations and the landing wait), not how long a job stayed open. Every figure prints a basis line under it. `Records::load` gains a `landings` field, read from the records branch the same way `gh/records.rs` reads it. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core status`: 33 passed, including the six new tests, which build real `athena_data::history::Landing` records and no HostError. The new tests for criteria 1, 3 and 4 would fail on the base code. The CHANGELOG and the hestia.rs prompt name the landing record, and I found no remaining claim that the CI wait has no record. Only the four listed files changed. Findings are minor: no test covers how `Records::load` reads `landings/` from the records branch; every `Records::load` call now reads the local records branch whatever tree it was asked to load, adding git calls and mixing that branch into loads of other trees; and one old test comment is stale.
